title: 'The Open Boat' by Stephen Crane, Part One
titleZh: 《海上扁舟》,斯蒂芬·克莱恩著,第一部分

sentences.en: Our story today is called “The Open Boat.”
sentences.zh: 我们今天的故事叫做《敞开的船》。

sentences.en: It was written by Stephen Crane and is based on what really happened to him in eighteen ninety-six.
sentences.zh: 它由斯蒂芬·克兰所写，基于他在1896年真实经历的事情。

sentences.en: Crane was traveling from the United States to Cuba as a newspaper reporter.
sentences.zh: 克兰当时正以记者的身份从美国前往古巴。

sentences.en: One night, his ship hit a sandbar.
sentences.zh: 一天夜里，他的船撞上了沙洲。

sentences.en: It sank in the Atlantic Ocean, off the coast of Florida.
sentences.zh: 船在大西洋沉没，地点在佛罗里达海岸附近。

sentences.en: Most of the people on board got into lifeboats.
sentences.zh: 船上大多数人登上了救生艇。

sentences.en: Crane was among the last to leave.
sentences.zh: 克兰是最后离开的人之一。

sentences.en: There were three others with him: the ship’s captain, the cook, and a sailor.
sentences.zh: 与他一起的还有三人：船上的船长、厨师和一名水手。

sentences.en: These four men climbed into the only remaining lifeboat.
sentences.zh: 这四个男人爬进了唯一剩下的那艘救生艇。

sentences.en: The boat was so small that no one believed it could stay afloat for very long.
sentences.zh: 艇太小了，没人相信它能长时间漂浮。

sentences.en: None of the four men thought he would ever reach the shore.
sentences.zh: 这四个男人中没有一个认为自己能到达岸边。

sentences.en: But the men fought the seas bravely, with all their strength.
sentences.zh: 但男人们竭尽全力勇敢地与风浪搏斗。

sentences.en: Would they finally reach land?
sentences.zh: 他们最终能登上陆地吗？

sentences.en: Here is Shep O’Neal with the first part of the story.
sentences.zh: 以下是谢普·奥尼尔带来的故事的第一部分。

sentences.en: The small lifeboat bounced from wave to wave in the rough seas of the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 那艘小小的救生艇在西洋汹涌的海浪间起伏颠簸。

sentences.en: The four men in the boat could not see the sky.
sentences.zh: 艇中的四个男人看不见天空。

sentences.en: The waves rose too high.
sentences.zh: 浪太高了。

sentences.en: The waves with their white tops pushed at the open boat with angry violence.
sentences.zh: 带着白色浪尖的海浪以愤怒的力量推挤着那艘敞开的船。

sentences.en: Every man thought each wave would be his last.
sentences.zh: 每个人都以为每一道浪都会是最后一道。

sentences.en: Surely, the boat would sink and he would drown.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，船会沉没，他也会溺亡。

sentences.en: The men thought that most adults would need a bathtub larger than the boat they were sailing.
sentences.zh: 男人们认为，大多数成年人需要的浴缸会比他们乘坐的这艘船还要大。

sentences.en: The waves were huge, and each created a problem in guiding the direction of the boat.
sentences.zh: 海浪巨大，每一道浪都给掌舵指引船的方向带来了困难。

sentences.en: For two days, since the ship sank, the four men had been struggling to reach land.
sentences.zh: 自船沉没以来，这四名男子已苦苦挣扎了两天，想要抵达陆地。

sentences.en: But there was no land to be seen.
sentences.zh: 然而却看不到任何陆地的踪影。

sentences.en: All the men saw were violent waves which rose and came fiercely down on them.
sentences.zh: 他们所能看到的，只有翻腾的巨浪，它们腾空而起，又猛烈地砸向他们。

sentences.en: The men sat in the boat, wondering if there was any hope for them.
sentences.zh: 男人们坐在船里，揣测着自己是否还存有希望。

sentences.en: The ship’s cook sat in the bottom of the boat.
sentences.zh: 船的厨师坐在船底。

sentences.en: He kept looking at the fifteen centimeters which separated him from the ocean.
sentences.zh: 他不停地望着自己与海洋之间那十五厘米的距离。

sentences.en: The boat had only two wooden oars.
sentences.zh: 这艘船只有两支木桨。

sentences.en: They were so thin – it seemed as if they would break against the waves.
sentences.zh: 它们太细了——看起来仿佛一碰到海浪就会折断。

sentences.en: The sailor, named Billie, directed the boat’s movement with one of the oars.
sentences.zh: 名叫比利的水手用其中一支桨控制着船的航行方向。

sentences.en: The newspaper reporter pulled the second oar.
sentences.zh: 那位报纸记者划着另一支桨。

sentences.en: He wondered why he was there in the boat.
sentences.zh: 他暗自纳闷，自己为什么会在这艘船里。

sentences.en: The fourth man was the captain of the ship that had sunk.
sentences.zh: 第四名男子正是那艘沉船船长。

sentences.en: He lay in the front of the small boat.
sentences.zh: 他躺在小船的前部。

sentences.en: His arm and leg were hurt when the ship sank.
sentences.zh: 船沉没时，他的手臂和腿都受了伤。

sentences.en: The captain’s face was sad.
sentences.zh: 船长的脸上满是悲伤。

sentences.en: He had lost his ship and many of his sailors.
sentences.zh: 他失去了自己的船，也失去了许多水手。

sentences.en: But he looked carefully ahead, and he told Billie when to turn the boat.
sentences.zh: 然而，他仍仔细地注视着前方，并在该转向时告诉比利。

sentences.en: “Keep her a little more south, Billie,” he said.
sentences.zh: “再往南偏一点，比利，”他说。

sentences.en: “A little more south, sir,” the sailor repeated.
sentences.zh: “再往南一点，先生，”水手重复道。

sentences.en: Sitting in the boat was like sitting on a wild horse.
sentences.zh: 坐在小船上，就像骑在一匹野马背上。

sentences.en: As each wave came, the boat rose and fell, like a horse starting toward a fence too high to jump.
sentences.zh: 随着每一道浪涌来，小船随浪起伏，宛如一匹马朝着高得无法逾越的栅栏奋起奔跃。

sentences.en: The problem was that after successfully floating over one wave you find that there is another one behind it just as strong and ready to flood your boat.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，当你好不容易成功浮越一道浪之后，却发现后面紧跟着另一道同样猛烈、随时会灌满小船的浪。

sentences.en: As each wall of water came in, it hid everything else that the men could see.
sentences.zh: 随着每一堵水墙涌来，它把船员们所能看见的其他一切都遮蔽了。

sentences.en: The waves came in silence; only their white tops made threatening noises.
sentences.zh: 浪涛无声地涌来，只有那白色的浪尖发出威胁般的咆哮。

sentences.en: In the weak light, the faces of the men must have looked gray.
sentences.zh: 在微弱的光线下，船员们的脸色想必是苍白的。

sentences.en: Their eyes must have shone in strange ways as they looked out at the sea.
sentences.zh: 当他们凝望大海时，他们的眼睛想必闪烁着奇异的光芒。

sentences.en: The sun rose slowly into the sky.
sentences.zh: 太阳缓缓升上天空。

sentences.en: The men knew it was the middle of the day because the color of the sea changed from slate gray to emerald green, with gold lights.
sentences.zh: 船员们知道已是正午，因为海水的颜色从板岩般的灰暗变成了翡翠般的碧绿，闪烁着金色的光芒。

sentences.en: And the white foam on the waves looked like falling snow.
sentences.zh: 浪尖上的白色泡沫看起来宛如飘落的雪花。

sentences.en: As the lifeboat bounced from the top of each wave, the wind tore through the hair of the men.
sentences.zh: 当小船从每一道浪尖上腾空跃起时，风穿过船员们的头发。

sentences.en: As the boat dropped down again the water fell just past them.
sentences.zh: 当小船再次坠落时，海水从他们身旁略过。

sentences.en: The top of each wave was a hill, from which the men could see, for a brief period, a wide area of shining sea.
sentences.zh: 每一道浪的浪尖都是一座山丘，船员们能借此在短暂的时间内望见一片广阔而波光粼粼的大海。

sentences.en: The cook said the men were lucky because the wind was blowing toward the shore.
sentences.zh: 厨师说船员们很幸运，因为风正朝着海岸的方向吹。

sentences.en: If it started blowing the other way, they would never reach land.
sentences.zh: 如果风转而朝另一个方向吹，他们就永远也到不了陆地了。

sentences.en: The reporter and the sailor agreed.
sentences.zh: 记者和水手都同意这一点。

sentences.en: But the captain laughed in a way that expressed humor and tragedy all in one.
sentences.zh: 但船长却以一种同时蕴含着幽默与悲剧的方式笑了起来。

sentences.en: He asked: “Do you think we’ve got much of a chance now, boys?”
sentences.zh: 他问道：“你们说，先生们，我们现在还有多少胜算呢？”

sentences.en: This made the others stop talking.
sentences.zh: 这话让其他人停止了交谈。

sentences.en: To express any hope at this time they felt to be childish and stupid.
sentences.zh: 在这个时候，他们觉得抱有任何希望都是幼稚而愚蠢的。

sentences.en: But they also did not want to suggest there was no hope.
sentences.zh: 但他们也不想让人以为毫无希望。

sentences.en: So they were silent.
sentences.zh: 所以他们沉默了。

sentences.en: “Oh, well,” said the captain, “We’ll get ashore all right.”
sentences.zh: “哦，好吧，”船长说，“我们会平安上岸的。”

sentences.en: But there was something in his voice that made them think, as the sailor said: “Yes, if this wind holds!”
sentences.zh: 但他的语气里有些东西让他们想起水手说的那句话：“是啊，只要这风不停！”

sentences.en: Seagulls flew near and far.
sentences.zh: 海鸥在近处和远处飞翔。

sentences.en: Sometimes the birds sat down on the sea in groups, near brown seaweed that rolled on the waves.
sentences.zh: 有时，鸟儿成群地落在海上，落在随波起伏的褐色海藻附近。

sentences.en: The anger of the sea was no more to them than it was to a group of chickens a thousand miles away on land.
sentences.zh: 大海的愤怒对它们而言，就像对千里之外陆地上一群鸡一样，毫无意义。

sentences.en: Often the seagulls came very close and stared at the men with black bead-like eyes.
sentences.zh: 有时，海鸥飞得非常近，用如黑豆般的小眼睛盯着这些人。

sentences.en: The men shouted angrily at them, telling them to be gone.
sentences.zh: 这些人愤怒地向它们吼叫，叫它们滚开。

sentences.en: The sailor and the reporter kept rowing with the thin wooden oars.
sentences.zh: 水手和记者用那薄薄的木桨不停地划着。

sentences.en: Sometimes they sat together, each using an oar.
sentences.zh: 有时，他们一起坐下，每人划一支桨。

sentences.en: Sometimes one would pull on both oars while the other rested.
sentences.zh: 有时，一个人会同时划动两支桨，而另一个人则休息。

sentences.en: Brown pieces of seaweed appeared from time to time.
sentences.zh: 褐色的海藻碎片不时出现。

sentences.en: They were like islands, bits of earth that did not move.
sentences.zh: 它们宛如岛屿，是那些不会移动的陆地碎片。

sentences.en: They showed the men in the boat that it was slowly making progress toward land.​
sentences.zh: 它们让船里的人们看到，小船正缓慢地朝着陆地前进。

sentences.en: Hours passed.
sentences.zh: 时间一分一秒地过去。

sentences.en: Then, as the boat was carried to the top of a great wave, the captain looked across the water.
sentences.zh: 然后，当小船被托起于一道巨浪之巅时，船长望向水面。

sentences.en: He said that he saw the lighthouse at Mosquito Inlet.
sentences.zh: 他说他看到了蚊子湾的灯塔。

sentences.en: The cook also said he saw it.
sentences.zh: 厨师也说看到了。

sentences.en: The reporter searched the western sky.
sentences.zh: 记者望向西方的天空。

sentences.en: “See it?” said the captain.
sentences.zh: “看见了吗?”船长说。

sentences.en: “No,” said the reporter slowly, “I don’t see anything.”
sentences.zh: “没有，”记者缓缓地说，“我什么也看不见。”

sentences.en: “Look again,” said the captain. He pointed.
sentences.zh: “再看一遍，”船长说。他指了一下。

sentences.en: “It’s exactly in that direction.”
sentences.zh: “就在那边的方向。”

sentences.en: This time the reporter saw a small thing on the edge of the moving horizon.
sentences.zh: 这一次，记者看见移动的地平线边缘有个小东西。

sentences.en: It was exactly like the point of a pin.
sentences.zh: 它正好像一枚针尖。

sentences.en: “Think we’ll make it, captain?” he asked.
sentences.zh: “我们大概能赶到吧，船长?”他问道。

sentences.en: “If this wind holds and the boat doesn’t flood, we can’t do much else,” said the captain.
sentences.zh: “只要这风不停，船不进水，我们就别无他法了，”船长说。

sentences.en: It would be difficult to describe the brotherhood of men that was here established on the sea.
sentences.zh: 很难用言语形容此刻在这片海上形成的人与人之间的兄弟情谊。

sentences.en: Each man felt it warmed him.
sentences.zh: 每个人都感到它给自己带来了温暖。

sentences.en: They were a captain, a sailor, a cook and a reporter.
sentences.zh: 他们中有一个人是船长，一个人是水手，一个人是厨师，还有一个是记者。

sentences.en: And they were friends.
sentences.zh: 而他们成了朋友。

sentences.en: The reporter knew even at the time that this friendship was the best experience of his life.
sentences.zh: 记者当时就知道，这份友谊是他一生中最美好的经历。

sentences.en: All obeyed the captain.
sentences.zh: 所有人都服从船长。

sentences.en: He was a good leader.
sentences.zh: 他是个优秀的领导者。

sentences.en: He always spoke in a low voice and calmly.
sentences.zh: 他总是压低声音、平静地说话。

sentences.en: “I wish we had a sail,” he said, “to give you two boys a chance to rest.”
sentences.zh: “真希望我们有一面帆，”他说，“好让你这两个孩子有个喘息的机会。”

sentences.en: So they used his coat and one of the oars to make a sail and the boat moved much more quickly.
sentences.zh: 于是他们拿他的外套和一支桨做成帆，船便快了许多。

sentences.en: The lighthouse had been slowly growing larger.
sentences.zh: 那座灯塔正慢慢变大。

sentences.en: At last, from the top of each wave the men in the boat could see land.
sentences.zh: 最后，从每一道浪峰上，船里的人能看到陆地了。

sentences.en: Slowly, the land seemed to rise from the sea.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，陆地似乎从海中升起。

sentences.en: Soon, the men could see two lines, one black and one white.
sentences.zh: 很快，人们能看到两条线，一条黑色，一条白色。

sentences.en: They knew that the black line was formed by trees, and the white line was the sand.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，黑线是树木形成的，白线则是沙滩。

sentences.en: At last, the captain saw a house on the shore.
sentences.zh: 最后，船长在岸上看到了一座房子。

sentences.en: And the lighthouse became even larger.
sentences.zh: 而灯塔变得更大。

sentences.en: “The keeper of the lighthouse should be able to see us now,” said the captain.
sentences.zh: “灯塔看守人现在应该能看到我们了，”船长说。

sentences.en: “He’ll notify the life-saving people.”
sentences.zh: “他会通知救生人员的。”

sentences.en: Slowly and beautifully, the land rose from the sea.
sentences.zh: 缓慢而美丽地，陆地从海中升起。

sentences.en: The wind came again.
sentences.zh: 风又刮了起来。

sentences.en: Finally, the men heard a new sound – the sound of waves breaking and crashing on the shore.
sentences.zh: 终于，人们听到了一种新的声音——海浪拍打并撞击岸边的声音。

sentences.en: “We’ll never be able to make the lighthouse now,” said the captain.
sentences.zh: “我们现在是到不了灯塔了，”船长说。

sentences.en: “Swing her head a little more north, Billie.”
sentences.zh: “再往北偏一点船头，比利。”

sentences.en: “A little more north, sir,” said the sailor.
sentences.zh: “再往北偏一点，先生，”水手说。

sentences.en: The men watched the shore grow larger.
sentences.zh: 人们望着岸边变得越来越大。

sentences.en: They became hopeful.
sentences.zh: 他们心中燃起了希望。

sentences.en: In an hour, perhaps, they would be on land.
sentences.zh: 也许再过一小时，他们就能踏上陆地了。

sentences.en: The men struggled to keep the boat from turning over.
sentences.zh: 人们努力防止翻船。

sentences.en: They were used to balancing in the boat.
sentences.zh: 他们早已习惯在船中保持平衡。

sentences.en: Now they rode this wild horse of a boat like circus men.
sentences.zh: 如今，他们像马戏团演员一样驾驭着这匹“野马”般的船。

sentences.en: The water poured over them.
sentences.zh: 水从他们身上倾泻而下。

sentences.en: The reporter thought he was now wet to the skin.
sentences.zh: 记者以为他现在已经湿透了。

sentences.en: But he felt in the top pocket of his coat and found eight cigars.
sentences.zh: 但他摸到外套顶部的口袋，发现八支雪茄。

sentences.en: Four were wet, but four were still dry.
sentences.zh: 四支湿了，但四支还是干的。

sentences.en: One of the men found some dry matches.
sentences.zh: 其中一名男子找到了一些干的火柴。

sentences.en: Each man lit a cigar.
sentences.zh: 每个男人都点燃了一支雪茄。

sentences.en: The four men sailed in their boat with the belief of a rescue shining in their eyes.
sentences.zh: 这四个男人划着船，眼中闪烁着获救的信念。

sentences.en: They smoked their big cigars and took a drink of water.​
sentences.zh: 他们抽着大雪茄，喝了几口水。

glossary.def: a small boat that is carried on a ship and that is used for saving the lives of the passengers and crew if the ship sinks
a type of plant that grows in the sea
a long pole that is flat and wide at one end and that is used for rowing and steering a boat
on or to the shore of an ocean, sea, lake, or river
feelings of friendship, support, and understanding between people
